extraction.name: CommonCatalog
extraction.description: A dataset of roughly 70 million open-licensed Creative-Commons images paired with high-quality synthetic captions generated using BLIP-2.
extraction.creator: Aaron Gokaslan; A. Feder Cooper; Jasmine Collins; Landan Seguin; Austin Jacobson; Mihir Patel; Jonathan Frankle; Cory Stephenson; Volodymyr Kuleshov
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was built by starting from YFCC100M metadata, re-scraping high-resolution Creative-Commons images from Flickr using the provided IDs, excluding non-derivative licenses, dividing the remaining images into commercial and non-commercial subsets, and generating synthetic captions for all images using a pre-trained BLIP-2 model.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Most Creative-Commons images lacked the captions needed for text-to-image training; only about 31% had alt text.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: High-resolution Creative-Commons images re-scraped from Flickr using IDs from the YFCC100M dataset; synthetic captions were generated for these images.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Images with non-derivative licenses were excluded, and the remaining images were split into commercial and non-commercial subsets.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For caption generation, all images were center-cropped and resized to a maximum of 512x512 pixels; diffusion model training used images at native resolution.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Synthetic captions were generated automatically using the pre-trained BLIP-2 OPT2.5B model for all Creative-Commons images.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The authors qualitatively compared captioning models, selected BLIP-2 based on qualitative analysis and MS COCO performance, and noted that BLIP-2 captions were often more descriptive than LAION alt-text but had reduced diversity.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors plan future augmentation of CommonCatalog with Creative-Commons images from other sources.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Images may depict faces, individual people, and noteworthy public figures/celebrities.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended as an alternative to web-scraped datasets with unclear copyright provenance, aiming to support more reproducible and open text-to-image training using Creative-Commons licensed data.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Synthetic captions may reduce caption diversity and web-sourced conceptual captions may not align with human-generated language nuances; the dataset is also about a decade old.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset has relatively few high-resolution CC images compared to LAION, most source images lacked captions, synthetic captions reduce diversity, and the underlying YFCC100M source is about a decade old and less current than LAION-2B.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training text-to-image diffusion models; the dataset was used to train the CommonCanvas family of latent diffusion models.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: The use of web-scraped data is a very common practice for training generative models, however, US courts have yet to definitively rule if this is permissible under copyright law ... Is it possible to efficiently produce a high-quality T2I model by training only on Creative-Commons-licensed data? ... One could instead independently curate a dataset of CC-licensed images with known provenance that expressly allow for copying, adaptation, and commercial use. As constituent images can be stored and distributed, this would also solve the link rot problem, thereby enabling greater reproducibility.
